rows.title: Star-target p-monotonicity conjecture for H-chromatic symmetric functions
rows.statement:
Let $n \geq 1$, let $H=S_{n+1}$ be a star, and let $G$ be any graph. Write $\omega$ for the standard involution on the ring of symmetric functions, and say that a symmetric function is **$p$-monotone** when all coefficients in its power-sum expansion are non-negative or all are non-positive.

**Star-target p-monotonicity conjecture.** The symmetric function $\omega(X_G^H)$ is $p$-monotone for every graph $G$.

This extends a known $p$-positivity phenomenon for ordinary chromatic symmetric functions to the $H$-chromatic setting, where the analogous statement does not hold for arbitrary $H$. The claim is presented as an open conjecture for star graphs.
rows.source_name: Nancy Mae Eagles, Angèle M. Foley, Alice Huang, Elene Karangozishvili and Annan Yu, “H-chromatic symmetric functions”, arXiv:2011.06063 (2021).
rows.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.06063

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

rows.title: Asymptotically optimal degree balance in regular graphs
rows.statement:
Let $G$ be a $d$-regular graph of order $n$, and let $m(H,k)$ denote the number of vertices of degree $k$ in a spanning subgraph $H$. **Asymptotic degree-balance conjecture.** For every $d$ there is a finite family $\mathcal{D}_d$ of exceptional graphs such that every $d$-regular graph $G$ of order $n$ not belonging to $\mathcal{D}_d$ has a spanning subgraph $H$ for which, for every integer $k$ with $0\leq k\leq d$, if $\frac{n}{d+1}$ and $\left\lceil\frac d2\right\rceil$ are odd integers, then

$$
\left|m(H,k)-\frac{n}{d+1}\right|\leq 1;
$$

otherwise,

$$
\left|m(H,k)-\frac{n}{d+1}\right|\leq \frac{d}{d+1}
$$

when $d$ is even, and

$$
\left|m(H,k)-\frac{n}{d+1}\right|\leq \frac{d-1}{d+1}
$$

when $d$ is odd. This conjecture refines the degree-balance problem by asserting that, apart from finitely many exceptions for each $d$, the parity obstruction is the only obstruction to attaining the bound $1$. The source explicitly notes that even the case $d=4$ is open.
rows.source_name: Borut Lužar, Jakub Przybyło and Roman Soták, “Degree-balanced decompositions of cubic graphs”, arXiv:2408.16121 (2025).
rows.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.16121

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2024). “We reckon even the case of $d=4$ constitutes an interesting open problem.”

rows.title: The cycle in an out-neighbourhood conjecture
rows.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and $T$ a tournament on the same vertex set. For a vertex $v$, write $N_T^+(v)$ for its out-neighbourhood in $T$.

**Cycle in an out-neighbourhood conjecture.** For every graph $G$ with sufficiently large chromatic number and every tournament $T$ on the same vertex set, there exists a vertex $v$ such that $G[N_T^+(v)]$ contains a cycle.

The paper presents this as an unresolved question in the setting where chromatic number is replaced by degeneracy and conjectures the displayed cycle-forcing statement as the case corresponding to degeneracy $2$; it also notes counterexamples for certain highly structured tournaments.
rows.source_name: António Girão, Kevin Hendrey, Freddie Illingworth, Florian Lehner, Lukas Michel, Michael Savery and Raphael Steiner, “Chromatic number is not tournament-local”, arXiv:2305.15585 (2023).
rows.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15585

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2023). “This conjecture remained open for two decades and was first proved by Lov\'{a}sz using homotopy theory (see also B\'{a}r\'{a}ny and Greene for very short proofs).”

purpose: Focused sustained proof or counterexample attempts on three problems whose literal statements are finite
